title: Checkpoint: SOLID Principles
intro: Review the five SOLID principles through changes to Python classes, interfaces, and dependencies.

questions.question: What are the reasons to change for this Order class?
questions.code:
class Order:
    def __init__(self, items):
        self.items = items
        self.total_price = self.calculate_total()
        self.total_price = self.apply_discount(self.total_price)
        self.save()
    def calculate_total(self): ...
    def apply_discount(self, total): ...
    def save(self): ...
options: Only one: everything in it is about orders
Three: the pricing formula, the discount rules and the storage
Its __init__ method, because it calls the other methods
None, as long as the class has tests
questions.explanation: Pricing, discounts and saving each change for their own reasons, often at the request of different people. SRP gives each one its own class: PriceCalculator, DiscountApplier and OrderRepository.

questions.question: After the SRP refactoring, the shop moves its orders from a database to a CSV file. Which class changes?
options: Order
PriceCalculator
OrderRepository
DiscountApplier
questions.explanation: Saving orders is OrderRepository's one job, so a new storage backend changes only that class. Order, PriceCalculator and DiscountApplier stay as they are.

questions.question: What has to change to support a Triangle?
options: Nothing: Triangle only needs an area() method
Only the TypeError message
Rectangle and Circle, which must get a common base class first
AreaCalculator.calculate, which needs a new isinstance branch
questions.explanation: The calculator checks each supported type directly. Adding a triangle to this version requires another branch in calculate.

questions.question: Which statement describes the Open/Closed Principle?
options: You add new behavior by adding new code, such as a subclass, without editing code that already works
A class must not get new subclasses once it is released, so its behavior stays fixed
Every attribute of a class should be private, so other code cannot modify it
A class may be modified only by its original author, never by other developers
questions.explanation: Open for extension, closed for modification: with a Shape base class that defines area(), a Triangle is one new subclass and no existing class changes.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
class Rectangle:
    def __init__(self, width, height):
        self._width, self._height = width, height
    def set_width(self, width): self._width = width
    def set_height(self, height): self._height = height
    def area(self): return self._width * self._height
class Square(Rectangle):
    def __init__(self, side): super().__init__(side, side)
    def set_width(self, width): self._width = self._height = width
    def set_height(self, height): self._width = self._height = height
sq = Square(5)
sq.set_width(5)
sq.set_height(10)
print(sq.area())
options: AssertionError
questions.explanation: Square.set_height also changes the width, so the area is 10 * 10. Code written for a Rectangle expects 50, so a Square cannot stand in for a Rectangle.

questions.question: Which design lets callers that only need area() use either Square or Rectangle?
options: Make Rectangle inherit from Square instead
Make both inherit from a Shape abstraction with area(), and neither from the other
Check isinstance(rect, Square) at the start of resize_rectangle
Make Square raise NotImplementedError in set_width and set_height
questions.explanation: Code that relies only on Shape.area() can use either shape. Code that requires Rectangle’s independent setters still cannot use Square.

questions.question: Robot inherits from a Worker ABC with work(), eat() and sleep(), and its eat() and sleep() only raise NotImplementedError. What is the problem?
options: Robot is forced to implement methods it does not use, so Worker should be split into smaller interfaces
Worker should not be an abstract class, because an ABC may have only one abstract method
Robot should inherit from Human, which already implements eat() and sleep()
eat() and sleep() should return None instead of raising, so callers do not crash
questions.explanation: The robot is required to provide operations it cannot honor. Give work, eating, and sleeping separate interfaces. Robot only needs Workable.

questions.question: assign_task(worker) only calls worker.work(). Which signature depends on the least while still accepting both Human and Robot?
options: def assign_task(worker: Human) -> None
def assign_task(worker: Human | Robot) -> None
def assign_task(worker: Eatable) -> None
def assign_task(worker: Workable) -> None
questions.explanation: A function should ask only for the methods it calls. With Workable, a new kind of worker such as a drone works with no change, while Human | Robot would need editing.

questions.explanation: The ABCs in collections.abc are small interfaces: Sized needs only __len__, Iterable only __iter__. Queue has just __len__, so it is Sized but not Iterable.

questions.question: Why is process() hard to test without charging a real card here?
options: PaymentProcessor creates CreditCardPayment itself, so a test cannot pass in a fake
process() returns None, so a test has nothing to compare against
CreditCardPayment has no base class, so a test cannot import it
amount is a float, so a test cannot compare it exactly
questions.explanation: The constructor creates the service. A test of this version can patch CreditCardPayment where it is looked up. With a constructor parameter, it can supply an object that records the amount.

questions.question: What happens when this code runs?
options: Paying $150.00 with credit card
TypeError: CreditCardPayment.pay() missing 1 required positional argument: 'amount'
Nothing is printed
AttributeError: type object 'CreditCardPayment' has no attribute 'pay'
questions.explanation: The class was passed instead of an object, so pay() is called on the class and 150.00 fills the self slot. Inject an object: PaymentProcessor(CreditCardPayment()).

questions.question: Which statement about the Dependency Inversion Principle is true?
options: Low-level classes such as CreditCardPayment should create the high-level classes that use them
Python needs a dependency injection framework before the principle can be applied
Every class needs an abstract base class, even when it has only one implementation
PaymentProcessor and the payment classes both depend on the Payment abstraction
questions.explanation: The processor depends on the payment operation. The concrete payment classes implement it. A caller chooses which implementation to pass in.
